subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Circling back on my earlier email about winning back lapsed riders for {Brand}. Since Ola ceased Australian operations in April 2024, share has concentrated toward Uber and DiDi, and the fight has moved from acquiring new riders to re-booking your existing base. With rider acquisition costs here running roughly 30 to 50 dollars per new rider, every dormant rider you revive instead of replace shifts the economics. We hold out a control group so the recovered rides read as incremental to your organic activity. Worth comparing against your current win-back mix?
angle: fresh angle: Ola April-2024 Australia exit consolidating share to Uber/DiDi (sourced) + rider CAC band $30-$50
register_notes: Stage 2 EN ride_hailing retargeting (Australia): acknowledges second follow-up and references prior email; fresh angle = timely development (Ola's April 2024 Australian exit concentrating share toward Uber and DiDi, web-verified via TechCrunch + The Conversation) plus real market CAC band $30-$50 per rider (financialmodelslab); names peer DiDi from brand_candidates (rotation); no MobUpps figure this stage, holdout incrementality referenced without a number; exactly one question mark; {Brand} and RECIPIENT_NAME kept; no sign-off; no em-dash; no hedge before a number; no 'X, not Y'; native register.
